title: From Skiplists to B+ Trees: A Memory-Efficient Sorted Set for PHP
topic: From Skiplists to B+ Trees: Making Valkey Sorted Sets More Memory Efficient
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints
description: We present a PHP implementation that transforms a skiplist-based sorted set into a B+ tree, achieving superior memory locality while preserving logarithmic s...
abstract: We present a PHP implementation that transforms a skiplist-based sorted set into a B+ tree, achieving superior memory locality while preserving logarithmic search, insertion, and deletion costs. The design retains the skiplist's simplicity but reorganizes nodes into a height-balanced B+ tree with leaf linkage for efficient range queries. Formal invariants guarantee that all leaves reside at the same depth and that each internal node contains between $\lceil m/2 \rceil$  and m children, where m is the order. Empirical evaluation on an Intel(R) Xeon(R) 6975P-C single-core Linux host yields a mean latency of 29 806 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 33 550 ops/s for 30 benchmark iterations. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/php-backend-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261122_030234_from_skiplists_to_b__trees__ma}.
